  4. How I'd verify each: Android Studio memory profiler heap dump (bitmap counts); Macrobenchmark with a 60-rail fixture; Perfetto for composition within frame; LeakCanary for retained states.
  5. Root cause: Cost scales with rails (outer composition) times items (inner), plus image memory; state wasn't keyed.
  6. Fix: Stable keys at both levels; per-rail rememberLazyListState() under the rail key (saved scroll position); contentType per rail kind; per-rail Paging or a windowed list (50 items becomes 12 plus load on scroll); Coil with exact size and memory cache limits; nested prefetch configured to a small count (the strategy details differ by foundation version: verify); @Immutable rail models and a mapper preserving instances; baseline profile.
items(rails, key = { it.id }, contentType = { it.kind }) { rail ->
    val state = rememberLazyListState()
    Rail(rail, state)
}
  1. Prevention: Memory and frame budgets in CI on a low-end device; JankStats and memory metrics in field by device class.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not prefetching aggressively on 3 GB devices (memory); not keeping all 60 rails' data in memory if rails can be refetched; TV needs focus handling beyond this scope.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• TV d-pad focus restore? → Focus requesters per rail with saved focused key; a separate topic.
  • 10 s network per rail? → Skeleton placeholders with fixed height to avoid layout shifts.
  • Rail count 200? → Outer list paging.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A composite: image memory, not Compose, caused OOM kills at 10x; once posters were decoded at display size the cost model of the lists barely mattered.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: "lazy handles it."
  • Hire: keys, per-rail state, windowing, image sizing.
  • Strong hire: ties memory/CPU budgets to device classes, verifies with profilers and benchmarks.

questions.contextHtml: Product asks: "Make the FAQ list expandable with a nice animation, and it should remember what the user opened." The FAQ has 120 items; some answers contain images and take 300 dp+ when expanded. After a prototype (animateContentSize on each row, remember for expanded), QA reports: expansion state is lost on scroll, the list jumps when expanding a row near the bottom, and after rotation everything is collapsed. The PM can't say whether "remember" means across scroll, across rotation, or across app restarts.
questions.promptHtml: How do you resolve the ambiguity and build it properly?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: Picks rememberSaveable without asking, ignoring process death or the jump.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Remember across scroll only, rotation, process death, or app restarts? Is accordion (one open) or multi-open? Does analytics need open events? Do we need deep link to an item expanded?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Hoist state out of the item now; scroll loss is a state-location bug.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) remember is disposed on scroll-out; (b) no rememberSaveable/ViewModel: rotation loss; (c) jump due to animateContentSize near viewport edge and lazy measure changes; (d) missing keys.
  4. How I'd verify each: Test each lifecycle: scroll away/back, rotate, adb shell am kill for process death, Layout Inspector for recomposition.
  5. Root cause: State lives in the item; the item lives only while on screen.
  6. Fix: Hold expandedIds: Set<Int> in the ViewModel using SavedStateHandle for process death (if agreed that's wanted), keyed items(faq, key = { it.id }). Animate with AnimatedVisibility/animateContentSize and apply Modifier.animateItem() for neighbours; for the jump, bringIntoViewRequester or animateScrollToItem after expansion if the item would extend offscreen.
val expanded by vm.expandedIds.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
items(faq, key = { it.id }) { q -> FaqRow(q, q.id in expanded, onToggle = { vm.toggle(q.id) }) }
  1. Prevention: Agree a written state-persistence matrix (scroll, rotate, process death, restart) for every list feature; tests for each row.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not persisting to disk without a product ask; not rememberSaveable per item for a shared concept like "collapse all" (needs hoisting).

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• "Collapse all" button? → Requires hoisted state; per-item state can't.
  • Accordion? → Single Int? instead of a set.
  • 120 items with images in each? → Images load lazily; expanded content composes only when visible.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A composite: a "remember what I opened" feature was built three times because nobody asked what "remember" meant; a one-line state matrix ended the churn.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: assumes and codes, leaves state in items.
  • Hire: asks the lifecycle question, hoists to ViewModel with keys.
  • Strong hire: state matrix, SavedStateHandle for process death, handles edge-of-viewport scroll.
